title: 🚀 Extension — Secure Login Simulation
subtitle: Build a login system with a 3-attempt lockout.
instructions: This is a build-it-yourself extension — there are no blanks to fill in. Write the login logic below the starter comments, using if/elif/else to handle three attempts (we'll learn a much neater way to do this with while loops next week).
starterCode:
# SECURE LOGIN SIMULATION - Morpheus Security Systems
# Stored credentials (in a real system these would be hashed!)
CORRECT_USERNAME = "agent_m"
CORRECT_PASSWORD = "Morpheus2024!"
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3

attempts = 0

print("=== MORPHEUS SECURITY SYSTEMS ===")
print("Please log in to continue.")
print()

# Your mission: write the login logic here
# It should:
#   - Ask for username and password
#   - Check if both are correct
#   - Count failed attempts
#   - Lock after MAX_ATTEMPTS failures
#   - Print a success or failure message each time

# HINT: while loops would make this neater, but we haven't learned them yet
# For now, use if/elif/else to handle the 3 attempt scenarios one at a time
hints: Start simple: ask for username and password, then check them with one if/else, just like Mission 2 in Lesson 1.
For attempt 2 and 3, you'll need to nest another if/elif/else inside the else of the one before it — it gets repetitive, which is exactly why while loops (next week) are so useful.
Use attempts to track how many failures have happened, and MAX_ATTEMPTS - attempts to work out how many tries are left.
Print 'Account LOCKED. Too many failed attempts.' once all 3 tries have failed.

codeChecks.message: Compare the entered username against CORRECT_USERNAME.
Compare the entered password against CORRECT_PASSWORD.
Track the number of failed attempts using the attempts variable.

successMessage: Nice work — that's a genuinely tricky exercise without loops! Test all three paths: success on try 1, success after 1-2 failures, and a full lockout after 3 failures.
